title: Cameras on Whale Sharks Helped Catalog 36 Behaviors

scenes.text: Scientists strapped cameras to whale sharks and mapped 36 behaviors.
The world's biggest fish, filmed from its own back fin, off Western Australia.
The cameras showed it feeding at every depth, down to about seventy meters.
When it hits a krill swarm, it switches from lazy drifting to a fast, vigorous chase.
Six of its feeding behaviors were new to science.
The tags fell off on their own after 24 hours. Now we can see how a giant eats.

description:
Scientists strapped cameras to whale sharks off Western Australia and catalogued 36 behaviors, using the footage and past studies.
The footage showed the biggest fish in the sea feeding at every depth, and six of its feeding behaviors were new to science.
What would you want to see through a whale shark's eyes?
first_comment: The cameras were set to fall off after 24 hours. What would you want to know about a whale shark's day?
